newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto to reject poll under Leghari.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto to reject poll under Leghari.

text.p: Pakistan's ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said on Tuesday she would not accept the result of next month's elections if held under President Farooq Leghari, who sacked her two months ago.

At a news conference held to issue a new election manifesto of her Pakistan People's Party (PPP), she opposed a presidential decree issued on Monday creating a new council that gives the armed forces a formal advisory role in government.
She said the decree was an attempt to drag the military into politics.
Bhutto said she would not boycott the February 3 polls, but her party was considering whether to begin protests before or after the vote.
She said the PPP would decide within 10 days whether to pursue a petition before the Supreme Court challenging her sacking on November 5 by Leghari on charges of corruption and misrule.

Bhutto said Leghari and his hand-picked caretaker government would seek to rig the elections to defeat the PPP and produce a hung parliament -- a situation which would allow the president to exercise all executive powers.

She said the PPP would win even if there were a semblance of fair elections. "But we know that the intelligence agencies have been directed to manipulate the election results, bring about a hung parliament so there can be puppet prime minister and (Leghari) can be president and de facto prime minister.

"What a pity for him that he can't declare himself chief of army staff. Otherwise, I am sure, he will put on a uniform and do that too," she said of her one-time protege who used a controversial constitutional provision to sack her.

Bhutto, who has called the charges against her false and malicious, accused Leghari of plunging Pakistan into political and economic crises, and said the only solution was a restoration of her government.
After that, she said, a meeting of major parties could decide whether there should be accountability before elections and who should supervise the next elections.

Bhutto said Leghari's 10-member Council for Defence and National Security, in which Paikstan's military elite will sit with the president, the prime minister and four ministers to advise the government, was totally unconstitutional.
"We believe that this is an attempt to drag the armed forces into politics by the president since the armed forces withdrew from politics in 1985 when non-party elections were held."

Bhutto said Leghari had gone even beyond late military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq to harm the parliamentary system of government by creating this council. She repeatedly called him "Farooq-ul-Haq".
"What even General Zia-ul-Haq was shamed into desisting from doing has now been accomplished by his present successor in power," Pakistan's human rights crusader Asma Jhangir said in a statement.
